content.title: I'm An April Fools' Baby & I'm Pulling These Genius Food Pranks This Year
content.text: These April Fool's Food Pranks Are TOO GOODDelish USLIVECurrent Time 0:03Total Duration 1:053 min readAs someone who was born on April Fools’ Day, I’m no stranger to a prank or two. Growing up, there was never a shortage of kids making jokes or pulling pranks on me to mark the occasion. While I certainly consider myself to have a good sense of humor, as a child it wasn't always fun to be the butt of a joke on your own birthday. Now that I'm an adult, it only seems fair to return the favor to those in my inner circle who helped me earn my badge of honor in my youth. Sleep with one eye open, people.Since my job revolves around food, I drew inspiration from the industry—and my childhood—to prank all of my unsuspecting friends and family this April Fools' Day. I hope you use these as inspiration to keep the holiday tradition alive. Happy fooling!Minty Oreosphotograph by dorisj//Getty ImagesWho doesn't love an Oreo? It's America's favorite sandwich cookie for a reason. Only a crazy person would turn one down, and that's exactly what we're banking on for this prank. Simply scrape out the cream filling or an Oreo or two and replace it with toothpaste. It looks exactly the same, but it might give whoever bites into it a shocking surprise. But hey, at least they'll have fresh breath!Sweet Grilled CheeseChelsea LupkinOne of my favorite weeks on Kids Baking Championship is when the kids are tasked with making dessert impostors. The challenge is to create a sweet dessert that masquerades as a classic savory dish and is so convincing that it could fool even Duff Goldman—or, at the very least, the recipient of your prank.Recreate a classic grilled cheese sandwich with two slices of browned pound cake, vanilla frosting, and a little food coloring. Or spoon some yogurt onto a plate in the shape of egg whites and top it with half of a fresh apricot to resemble sunny-side-up eggs. There are endless ways to turn your favorite dishes into something new with unconventional foods.Veggie CakeJGI/Jamie Grill//Getty ImagesKnow anyone else with an April Fools' birthday? A couple of years ago, my niece got me good by hiding a piece of broccoli in my birthday cake. It's an easy, low-lift prank that, thankfully, doesn't ruin the entire cake but it’ll still give the person on the receiving end quite a surprise. And some vitamins!Unspillable OJChelsea LupkinEver wanted to channel your inner housewife? The Bravo franchise is notorious for drink-throwing, and with this trick, you can live out that fantasy without actually getting anyone wet! I present: unspillable orange juice.Simply heat one cup of orange juice to a simmer, then turn off the heat and sprinkle in a packet of gelatin. Whisk until the gelatin has dissolved completely, then add one more cup of orange juice. Pour the mixture into a tall glass and add a straw for effect. Pop it in the fridge, and in 4 to 6 hours, you’ll be able to turn the whole thing upside down with no problem. It’s perfect for scaring people with white carpets or expensive electronics.Extra Cold Cerealmrs//Getty ImagesThere's nothing like starting your day with a big bowl of cereal. Prep your prank the night before by placing a filled bowl in the freezer. The cereal will harden into the milk, making it nearly impossible to scoop up a bite. Confusion will undoubtedly ensue when you serve it to your unsuspecting loved one in the morning.Advertisement - Continue Reading Below“Fruit” SnacksChelsea LupkinOf all of the tricks up my sleeve, this one is definitely the easiest. Do it for the Cadbury Egg lover in your life, and they may never forgive you. It's pretty self-explanatory: Buy some grapes and buy some Cadbury Eggs. Remove the eggs from their wrappers and replace them with grapes.If you’re feeling nice, you could save the chocolate eggs and give them to your prank victims as a reward for putting up with you. Or, you know, you could eat them all yourself. We won’t judge.
